subagent_reports.architecture_assessment: Core design is sound: restore upstream engineer-first routing, then reuse existing typed provenance, stable report identity, and reducer cycle guards. Highest leverage comes from one post-implementation follow-up funnel shared by delegated and inline success paths. Do not add another state machine, provenance union, preview schema, or designer-specific completion guard. Design still needs explicit packet/report wiring and semantic-test strengthening. Current designer neighboring-policy prose contradicts the approved same-surface alignment allowance and must be reconciled across synchronized surfaces.

validation.notes: Proceed after incorporating four low-risk contract-tied adjustments: shared follow-up funnel, direct reuse of returned reportId for engineer_report provenance, explicit apply_context packet/report requirements, and semantic lifecycle tests. Also reconcile current designer neighboring-policy prose with AC5. No security or release blocker found.

tradeoffs: One shared follow-up funnel reduces duplicated routing prose but makes that funnel a critical orchestration seam requiring delegated and inline scenario coverage.
Reusing existing optional apply_context preserves legacy report ingestion, but new engineer/designer packet contracts must make cycle context mandatory for this classified lifecycle.
Stronger semantic tests cost more fixture maintenance than substring checks, but prevent designer-direct regressions that token-presence tests miss.
Reusing design_dimensions.notes and verification avoids schema growth, but packet prose must state exactly where unavailable-preview rationale and source/a11y evidence belong.

alternatives_considered.option: Add a new designer-follow-up state machine or provenance variant
alternatives_considered.rationale: Existing apply cycle, provenance union, report identity, report persistence guard, and completion guard already encode required structure.

alternatives_considered.option: Duplicate follow-up dispatch separately in engineer and inline branches
alternatives_considered.rationale: A single post-success funnel is simpler and reduces drift between AC2 and AC3.

alternatives_considered.option: Reconstruct engineer report keys in orchestration prose
alternatives_considered.rationale: adv_subagent_report_submit already returns the canonical reportId.

alternatives_considered.option: Add dedicated unavailable-preview report fields
alternatives_considered.rationale: Existing verification entries and required notes for n/a or concern dimensions can carry bounded rationale and source/a11y evidence.

alternatives_considered.option: Retain token-presence routing tests
alternatives_considered.rationale: Current tests demonstrate that contradictory designer-direct and engineer-first descriptions can coexist while token checks pass.

architecture_judgement.recommendation: Auto-adopt four bounded adjustments: converge delegated and inline implementation success into one designer-follow-up packet builder/funnel; seed engineer apply_context with the active cycle and engineer provenance, then pass submit response reportId as designer engineer_report provenance; require designer apply_context in new classified follow-up packets/reports while retaining legacy schema compatibility; replace token-presence checks with semantic scenarios covering initial worker, ordering, delegated/inline provenance, stale-cycle rejection, and reviewer ownership. Synchronize adjacent same-surface alignment language. Treat new provenance/state/preview schema proposals as no-op.

subagent_reports.recommendation: Adopt shared follow-up funnel and existing typed mechanisms; strengthen packet contracts and semantic tests; reconcile adjacent-UI wording before validator review.
follow_ups: Episode recall returned no relevant project decision; conclusions rely on current repository source and packet-provided agreement.
lgrep semantic search timed out twice, including required hybrid:false retry; exact lgrep text search and targeted file reads provided source evidence.

No user-surface candidate identified: approved agreement resolves preview fallback and adjacent-alignment tradeoffs, and all recommended changes are contract-tied, low-risk design adjustments or explicit no-ops.

subagent_reports.architecture_assessment: Core shape is correct and simpler than adding another state machine or provenance variant: reuse the existing strict provenance union, consume returned reportId, and preserve reducer cycle guards (https://github.com/Sharper-Flow/Advance/blob/main/plugin/src/types/subagent-reports.ts#L82-L109; https://github.com/Sharper-Flow/Advance/blob/main/plugin/src/tools/subagent-report.ts#L694-L715; https://github.com/Sharper-Flow/Advance/blob/main/plugin/src/temporal/change-state.ts#L937-L963). However, design is not yet spec-law complete. Current routing gives Priority 1 metadata.delegation_hint precedence over frontend classification, while design implementation strategy explicitly mentions replacing only Priority 1.5; that leaves a path for an adv-designer hint to violate SC1/AC1/DONT1 unless precedence/allowed-hint semantics are explicitly changed and tested (https://github.com/Sharper-Flow/Advance/blob/main/.opencode/command/adv-apply.md#L406-L446). Design also lacks an explicit orchestrator transition for designer spawn/report failure, despite SC2 requiring incomplete state with explicit failure; report schemas can durably represent status:error, but packet/funnel handling must require that outcome and forbid completion (https://github.com/Sharper-Flow/Advance/blob/main/plugin/src/types/subagent-reports.ts#L230-L323).

blockers: Routing precedence is unresolved: current Priority 1 metadata.delegation_hint wins over metadata.frontend, and design only names replacement of Priority 1.5. Without explicit frontend-safe hint semantics plus a semantic regression case, initial direct adv-designer dispatch remains possible, violating SC1, AC1, and DONT1 (https://github.com/Sharper-Flow/Advance/blob/main/.opencode/command/adv-apply.md#L406-L446).

Designer follow-up failure handling is underspecified. SC2 requires explicit failure while remaining incomplete; existing status:error and completion guards provide primitives, but design must define funnel behavior for spawn failure, malformed/missing report, status:error, and submit failure, and test that no path marks task done (https://github.com/Sharper-Flow/Advance/blob/main/plugin/src/types/subagent-reports.ts#L298-L323; https://github.com/Sharper-Flow/Advance/blob/main/plugin/src/temporal/change-state.ts#L937-L963).
validation.notes: No security or release blocker found. Spec-law blockers should be resolved before design gate approval.

tradeoffs: One shared follow-up funnel reduces delegated/inline drift but becomes a mandatory orchestration choke point whose failure behavior must be explicit.
Keeping apply_context optional preserves legacy report readability, but correctness for new classified work must come from required packet contracts plus existing completion guards.
Reusing returned reportId avoids duplicate identity logic, but orchestrator must branch only on successful submit output and must not infer identity after submit failure.

alternatives_considered.option: Add a new workflow state machine or provenance union arm
alternatives_considered.rationale: Existing implementation_cycle_id, engineer/engineer_report/inline provenance, durable reportId, and reducer guards already encode required authority (https://github.com/Sharper-Flow/Advance/blob/main/plugin/src/types/subagent-reports.ts#L82-L109).

alternatives_considered.option: Keep designer-direct initial implementation
alternatives_considered.rationale: Contradicts approved SC1/AC1/DONT1 and current direct-routing law is the regression being corrected (https://github.com/Sharper-Flow/Advance/blob/main/.adv/specs/delegation-defaults/spec.json#L465-L518).

alternatives_considered.option: Separate engineer and inline designer packet builders
alternatives_considered.rationale: Equivalent lifecycle behavior with two builders creates avoidable drift; provenance is already the typed variation point (https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/main/packages/docs/content/api.mdx).

alternatives_considered.option: Make apply_context globally required in persisted schema
alternatives_considered.rationale: Would break stated legacy compatibility; current completion guard already prevents legacy unanchored reports from completing newly classified work (https://github.com/Sharper-Flow/Advance/blob/main/plugin/src/temporal/change-state.ts#L937-L963).

alternatives_considered.option: Preserve explicit delegation_hint precedence unchanged
alternatives_considered.rationale: Allows an adv-designer hint to bypass engineer-first lifecycle and conflicts with approved universal frontend classification behavior (https://github.com/Sharper-Flow/Advance/blob/main/.opencode/command/adv-apply.md#L406-L446).

architecture_judgement.recommendation: Do not approve design gate yet. Amend design to define metadata.frontend-safe Priority 1 hint handling and explicit follow-up failure transitions, then require semantic tests for frontend+adv-designer hint, designer spawn/report/submit failure, delegated provenance, inline provenance, stale/mismatched cycles, and reviewer ownership.

subagent_reports.recommendation: Retain core architecture, but close two spec-law gaps before planning: (1) explicitly prevent any metadata.delegation_hint from selecting adv-designer as initial worker for classified tasks, while preserving valid inline/risk semantics; (2) define and test explicit incomplete/error handling for every designer-follow-up failure mode. Keep existing provenance union, durable reportId, reducer guards, and optional-schema legacy compatibility.
follow_ups: After design amendment, rerun design validation against exact Priority 1 semantics and failure-path assertions.

Semantic tests must assert ordering and outcomes, not token presence; current weak test accepts contradictory law (https://github.com/Sharper-Flow/Advance/blob/main/plugin/src/delegation-matrix.test.ts#L726-L752).

subagent_reports.topic: Revalidation of revised engineer-first designer-follow-up design

sources.label: Revised approved design and agreement
sources.summary: Revision explicitly bounds Priority-1 hints to eligibility, requires engineer-first delegated classified work, routes successful delegated and inline implementation through one designer follow-up funnel, and defines no-completion structured recovery for dispatch/report/verification failures.

sources.label: Current routing precedence requiring change
sources.summary: Current source gives metadata.delegation_hint Priority 1 and direct designer routing Priority 1.5; revised DDC3 and implementation strategy now explicitly constrain this precedence for classified work.

sources.label: Existing typed provenance
sources.summary: Existing implementation_cycle_id plus engineer, engineer_report, and inline provenance variants support revised funnel without new schema arms.

sources.label: Existing report status and compatibility surface
sources.summary: Engineer/designer reports support complete/error status while apply_context remains optional for legacy compatibility; revised new-packet contract requires apply_context for classified follow-ups.

sources.label: Durable report identity output
sources.summary: Submit output returns stable reportId, including duplicate handling, supporting revised no-reconstruction requirement.

sources.label: Frontend completion guard
sources.summary: Task completion already requires a complete matching-cycle designer report, preventing unresolved designer failures or missing provenance from checkpointing done.

sources.label: Designer ownership and cycle-anchor rejection
sources.summary: Report/task ownership mismatches and stale or mismatched claimed designer cycles are rejected before persistence.

sources.label: Existing reducer regression evidence
sources.summary: Tests cover missing matching evidence, matching evidence, mismatched cycles, stale cycles, and stale duplicate resubmission.

subagent_reports.architecture_assessment: Revised design resolves both prior blockers. Priority-1 hints are now eligibility-only and cannot select the initial worker for metadata.frontend=true tasks, directly satisfying SC1/AC1/DONT1 at design level when paired with DDC3/DDC5 semantic tests (adv://change/restoreDesignerFollowUp; https://github.com/Sharper-Flow/Advance/blob/main/.opencode/command/adv-apply.md#L406-L446). Designer dispatch, malformed/error report, and verification failures now follow one explicit no-checkpoint recovery path with bounded remediation and unresolved retry/escalation, satisfying SC2 while relying on the existing matching-cycle completion authority (adv://change/restoreDesignerFollowUp; https://github.com/Sharper-Flow/Advance/blob/main/plugin/src/temporal/change-state.ts#L937-L963). AC4 is satisfied architecturally by requiring apply_context in every new classified follow-up packet, retaining stale/mismatch ingestion rejection, and preventing missing-context evidence from satisfying completion while preserving readability of legacy optional-context reports (https://github.com/Sharper-Flow/Advance/blob/main/plugin/src/types/subagent-reports.ts#L230-L323; https://github.com/Sharper-Flow/Advance/blob/main/plugin/src/temporal/change-state.ts#L1120-L1166).

validation.notes: Revised design satisfies SC1/AC1/DONT1 and SC2/AC4. Implementation must preserve the stated distinction between legacy readability and strict validation of new classified follow-up packets.

tradeoffs: Eligibility-only hints simplify classified worker ordering but intentionally reduce hint authority for frontend tasks.
A shared failure path reduces divergent behavior but requires semantic coverage across spawn, malformed report, status:error, submit, and verification failures.
Optional apply_context preserves legacy readability, while new classified packets and completion authority must enforce cycle context structurally.

alternatives_considered.option: Retain unrestricted Priority-1 worker selection
alternatives_considered.rationale: Would preserve a designer-direct bypass contrary to SC1/AC1/DONT1 (https://github.com/Sharper-Flow/Advance/blob/main/.opencode/command/adv-apply.md#L406-L446).

alternatives_considered.option: Add a new state machine or provenance arm
alternatives_considered.rationale: Existing typed provenance and completion guards already represent required ordering and authority (https://github.com/Sharper-Flow/Advance/blob/main/plugin/src/types/subagent-reports.ts#L82-L109).

alternatives_considered.option: Make apply_context globally mandatory in persisted schema
alternatives_considered.rationale: Would unnecessarily break legacy report readability; strict new packet validation plus matching-cycle completion guards provides a simpler compatibility boundary (https://github.com/Sharper-Flow/Advance/blob/main/plugin/src/types/subagent-reports.ts#L230-L323).

architecture_judgement.recommendation: Approve design gate. During planning/execution, require semantic tests for all supported Priority-1 hint values, missing/stale/mismatched apply_context, designer spawn/malformed/status:error/submit/verification failures, bounded remediation, and no checkpoint while unresolved.

subagent_reports.recommendation: Approve revised design. Preserve exact DDC3-DDC7 semantics in plan and tests; specifically prove missing apply_context is rejected for new classified follow-ups or otherwise cannot persist as valid new evidence, while legacy persisted reports remain readable.
follow_ups: Caution: AC4 wording says classified reports reject missing provenance. Tests should explicitly prove the chosen new-report boundary rejects missing apply_context, not merely that completion later fails, while legacy stored reports remain readable.
Caution: bounded remediation must have finite retry/escalation assertions so failure recovery cannot loop or silently complete.

sources.label: Current designer cycle guards
sources.summary: Designer evidence is checked by task and cycle, but engineer_report provenance report_key is not referentially validated here.

sources.summary: Report submission computes and returns stable reportId, including on duplicate success.

sources.summary: Frontend task completion already fails without same-cycle successful designer evidence.

sources.summary: Zod 4 documents strict objects for unknown-key rejection; safeParse provides explicit success/error branching.

sources.summary: Official sample uses a signal handler for simple deterministic Workflow-state mutation.

subagent_reports.architecture_assessment: Existing shape is sound: narrow change-owned delta intent, Temporal durable state, and archive-only global writes; engineer/designer evidence already has implementation-cycle anchoring. Bounded candidates, sorted by payoff/risk: (1) AUTO-ADOPT — export a modify-only schema/type and strengthen it with non-empty changes, delta/requirement ID validation, and target-consistent replacement scenario IDs; payoff high, risk low, ties AC8/DDC1, prior consideration new. (2) AUTO-ADOPT — when designer provenance kind is engineer_report, reducer must resolve report_key to a successful same-task, same-cycle adv-engineer report before persisting designer evidence; payoff high, risk low, ties AC2/AC4, prior consideration new. (3) AUTO-ADOPT — shared follow-up builder must consume reportId returned by adv_subagent_report_submit rather than reconstructing report keys; payoff medium, risk low, ties AC2/AC4, prior consideration new. (4) NO-OP — retain operation-specific Signal/store/read-back plumbing and existing task-completion guard; do not introduce Temporal Updates or a second designer-follow-up state machine for this restoration. Existing signal rejection records plus same-cycle completion guard provide the needed durable safety; payoff medium, risk low, ties AC8/AC2, prior consideration archived:updateSubagentDispatch/addSpecDeltaWriter. No user-value tradeoff candidate found, so nothing requires user surfacing.

validation.notes: Design direction is valid, but schema emptiness/scenario invariants and engineer_report referential integrity should be explicit design-derived criteria before implementation. Semantic search timed out twice; exact lgrep text/symbol search and direct source reads provided local evidence.

tradeoffs: Stronger modify refinements reject previously schema-valid no-op payloads, intentionally narrowing compatibility.
Referential engineer-report checks add reducer lookup/test work but prevent fabricated or stale report-key provenance.
Reusing Signals preserves one mutation pattern but does not provide Update-style synchronous result semantics; current signal-plus-query contract remains simpler for this bounded restoration.

alternatives_considered.option: Expose full add/modify/remove/rename CRUD
alternatives_considered.rationale: Exceeds approved modify-only scope and expands destructive safety surface.

alternatives_considered.option: Use Temporal Updates for adv_delta_modify
alternatives_considered.rationale: Updates provide validator-backed acceptance/results, but introducing a second message pattern is unnecessary while established signal-plus-authoritative-query behavior meets bounded change-owned recording needs.

alternatives_considered.option: Add a separate durable designer-follow-up workflow state machine
alternatives_considered.rationale: Existing apply_cycle, typed reports, signal rejections, and task-completion guard already encode ordering and incompletion structurally.

alternatives_considered.option: Trust non-empty engineer_report.report_key without lookup
alternatives_considered.rationale: String shape alone does not prove successful same-task, same-cycle engineer provenance.

architecture_judgement.recommendation: Adopt candidates 1-3 into design and tests; retain candidate 4 as explicit no-op. Proceed after adding criteria for non-empty/target-consistent modify payloads and referential engineer-report provenance.

subagent_reports.recommendation: Update design before planning: strengthen/export modify schema, require same-cycle engineer-report referential integrity, and mandate use of submit-returned reportId in the shared designer follow-up builder. Keep existing Signal/archive/completion architecture; no user decision needed.
follow_ups: Packet omitted STOP_WHEN and VERIFICATION anchors; research continued under supplied scope per transport contract and used evidence-backed source inspection.
Semantic lgrep search timed out with hybrid on and off; fallback exact lgrep search plus direct source reads succeeded.

subagent_reports.architecture_assessment: Design is structurally correct and simpler than alternatives. Modify-only adv_delta_modify reuses the existing typed modify variant, Store/Signal/Query/read-back lifecycle, and sole archive writer rather than introducing CRUD, direct spec edits, Temporal Updates, or a second archive engine (https://github.com/Sharper-Flow/Advance/blob/fa33e04c17579d5f56d3e8a2f13f6b063b1bcb48/plugin/src/archive/delta.ts; https://docs.temporal.io/develop/typescript/workflows/message-passing). Engineer-first then same-cycle designer follow-up aligns with existing implementation-cycle and report-key primitives, and returned reportId avoids heuristic key reconstruction (https://github.com/Sharper-Flow/Advance/blob/fa33e04c17579d5f56d3e8a2f13f6b063b1bcb48/plugin/src/tools/subagent-report.ts#L694-L715; https://github.com/Sharper-Flow/Advance/blob/fa33e04c17579d5f56d3e8a2f13f6b063b1bcb48/plugin/src/types/subagent-reports.ts#L82-L109). AC1-AC10, C1-C6, and DONT1-DONT5 are covered at design level. Two implementation-defining cautions must be made explicit before planning: (1) successful designer evidence must structurally require status=complete, empty blockers, and all required verification exit codes zero; current completion helper checks only status/task/cycle (https://github.com/Sharper-Flow/Advance/blob/fa33e04c17579d5f56d3e8a2f13f6b063b1bcb48/plugin/src/temporal/change-state.ts#L1092-L1105); (2) modify validation must run at both tool preflight and workflow reducer boundaries, verify the target exists in the named capability, reject empty changes, malformed/empty/duplicate scenario IDs and wrong scenario parents, and reject any existing same-target modify/remove/rename before state mutation. Strict/refined schemas are the canonical mechanism (https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/blob/v3.24.2/README.md).

validation.notes: No architecture blocker. Resolve two cautions in design-derived planning/tests: define the complete designer-success predicate, and enumerate reducer-level modify invariants/atomicity. Current packet omitted labeled TASK_SCOPE/IN_SCOPE/OUT_OF_SCOPE/DONE_WHEN/STOP_WHEN/VERIFICATION anchors; research continued under explicit user objective and this omission is recorded as a follow-up.

tradeoffs: A dedicated adv_delta_modify duplicates some adv_delta_add lifecycle plumbing, but preserves a narrow, discoverable, modify-only public contract and avoids widening the established add-only tool.
Strict pre-signal plus reducer validation adds duplicated checks, but protects Temporal replay/alternate callers and keeps malformed/conflicting writes out of durable change state.
Mandatory designer follow-up adds latency and a second worker/report dependency for every structurally classified frontend task, but provides enforceable UI quality and preserves reviewer ownership.
Referential integrity against returned reportId adds lookup and tests, but prevents spoofed, stale, reconstructed, or cross-task/cycle implementation provenance.

alternatives_considered.option: Expand adv_delta_add to accept add|modify
alternatives_considered.rationale: The tool name and accepted add-only contract would become misleading, existing add-only regression law would weaken, and callers would receive a broader mutation surface than needed.

alternatives_considered.option: Expose generic CRUD delta writer
alternatives_considered.rationale: Remove and rename semantics are unnecessary for AC8-AC9 and materially widen destructive/conflict behavior.

alternatives_considered.option: Directly edit rq-delDefaults10 in global spec files

## Cross-Project Origin

# Proposal: Restore designer follow-up

## Why
The accepted `updateSubagentDispatch` contract requires one initial code implementation lane (`adv-engineer`) and a subsequent design-focused pass (`adv-designer`) for explicitly classified UI/UX work. Current apply routing regressed to direct frontend implementation by `adv-designer`.

## What Changes
- Restore engineer-first dispatch for delegated code tasks, including explicitly classified UI/UX tasks.
- Run the designer after implementation for classified UI/UX work, with implementation-result and visual-context handoff.
- Reconcile command routing, worker packets, agent contracts, delegation specification, generated documentation, and regression coverage.

## User Outcomes
- UI work has predictable implementation ownership.
- Shipped interfaces receive a bounded, dedicated quality pass after code exists.
- Backend/business logic stays with engineering; review and hardening stay independent.

## Affected Code
- `.opencode/command/adv-apply.md`
- `.opencode/command/adv-prep.md`
- `.opencode/agents/adv-engineer.md`
- `.opencode/agents/adv-designer.md`
- delegation-defaults documentation and dispatch regression tests

## Related Repositories
- Advance source: `/home/jon/dev/advance`
- Deployed Advance artifacts remain deploy-script outputs.

## Constraints
- UI/UX classification must remain structural (`metadata.frontend`), not title/path inference.
- Designer follow-up receives engineer outcome and remains within frontend/UI scope.
- `adv-reviewer` remains sole review/harden owner.

## Impact
Classified UI/UX work gains an ordered quality pass after implementation. Non-UI code retains existing engineer routing.

## Scope
### In Scope
- Engineer-first UI/UX implementation routing.
- Ordered designer follow-up dispatch and packet context.
- Relevant agent/command/spec/documentation/test alignment.

### Out of Scope
- Model-routing policy.
- Product-facing UI implementation.
- Review/harden ownership changes.

### Must Not
- Must not route initial frontend implementation directly to `adv-designer`.
- Must not use filename, path, title, or prose heuristics as authoritative UI/UX classification.
- Must not give `adv-designer` backend, API, storage, or business-logic authority.

## Discovery Findings

### Discovery Checklist
| Step | Result | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Skills considered | PASS | `adv-agent-tool-contracts` loaded; no pending global skill review found. |
| Prior research extension | PASS | Archived `updateSubagentDispatch` and `docs/adv-agents-design-skills-prep.md` consulted. |
| Conflict scan | DEGRADED | Target inventory returned 95 changes but transport was truncated; no active same-purpose change observed in returned inventory. |
| Edge cases | PASS | Inline implementation, provenance, stale assertions, and delegation-hint behavior analyzed. |
| Design question depth | PASS | Questions are bounded below with trust model, blast radius, and alternatives. |
| Draft spec deltas | PASS | `rq-delDefaults10` restoration drafted below. |
| Related-pattern scan | PASS | Seven direct-designer routing/documentation/test surfaces found. |
| LBP check | PASS | Internal contract restoration; no external solution is viable or required. |
| Completeness verification | PASS | Multiple routing surfaces verified; no sole-entry claim is relied on. |

### Skills Considered
- `adv-agent-tool-contracts` — direct match; packet, typed-report, specification, and regression-test alignment is required.
- `adv-frontend-review` — relevant to designer quality bar but not to this dispatch-contract restoration; not loaded.

### Extends
- `updateSubagentDispatch` — accepted contract established engineer-first implementation and matching-cycle designer follow-up.
- `docs/adv-agents-design-skills-prep.md` — identified frontend routing metadata and need for structural quality evidence.
- New finding: commit `669f124a` on 2026-07-15 changed `rq-delDefaults10` from engineer-first to designer-direct while cycle-anchor guards remained aligned to a follow-up model.

### Conflict Scan
- `updateSubagentDispatch` is the relevant archived precedent.
- No active same-purpose restoration change was observed in the returned target inventory.
- Inventory completeness is degraded because the cross-project list response was truncated; discovery must not treat this as a clean global no-conflict assertion.

### Current State
- `.opencode/command/adv-apply.md` Priority 1.5 directly routes `metadata.frontend == "true"` to `adv-designer`.
- `ADV_INSTRUCTIONS.md`, worker contracts, prep guidance, the delegation documentation mirror, and regression assets repeat that direct-designer law.
- Reducer guards already require matching-cycle designer evidence before frontend task completion and reject stale designer-cycle evidence. They are the structural seam to preserve, not weaken.

### Edge Cases
1. Risk-forced inline UI implementation must still emit a designer follow-up packet with inline provenance; otherwise task completion blocks without a reachable follow-up.
2. Engineer-first dispatch must produce `engineer` provenance for the engineer report and `engineer_report` provenance for the designer follow-up; those schema arms are currently under-produced.
3. A stale matrix test comment currently says engineer-first while its assertions permit designer-direct behavior; assertions must test the semantic then-clauses.
4. `delegation_hint: "delegate_preferred"` must not bypass engineer-first ordering for classified UI/UX tasks.

### Open Design Questions
1. **Technical, agent-resolved.** How should inline UI work seed follow-up provenance? Trust: agent-only. Blast radius: blocked completion if wrong. Alternatives: use existing inline provenance arm; do not weaken cycle guards. Recommendation: existing inline arm.
2. **Technical, agent-resolved.** How should engineer and designer reports prove ordered handoff? Trust: agent-only. Blast radius: designer could appear first. Alternatives: new heuristic versus existing typed `engineer` and `engineer_report` provenance. Recommendation: wire existing typed arms and add packet/schema tests.
3. **Outcome scope, user confirmation needed.** Which classified UI/UX tasks require a designer pass, and whether unavailable visual verification may be explicitly deferred. Trust: joint. Blast radius: quality guarantees and blocked delivery. Alternatives are presented in the discovery questions.

### Draft Spec Deltas
- `rq-delDefaults10` — restore Engineer-First Frontend Dispatch.
  - Given a delegated code task with `metadata.frontend == "true"`, when apply dispatch begins, then the initial implementation worker is `adv-engineer`.
  - Given successful classified UI/UX implementation, when the engineer result is available, then a same-cycle `adv-designer` follow-up receives the engineer outcome and UI scope.
  - Given an inline classified UI/UX implementation, when implementation succeeds, then the designer follow-up receives bounded inline provenance.

### Related Pattern Scan
Direct-designer behavior repeats across the apply command, session routing instructions, prep metadata guidance, agent contracts, delegation documentation, and four regression assets. These are one policy family and must change together; no unrelated worker lane was found with the same UI lifecycle contract.

### Completeness Verification
- **Problem completeness — high confidence:** evidence identifies the regression commit, direct routing, packet semantics, and downstream cycle guards; this is more than a single prompt-text symptom.
- **Solution scope — high confidence:** routing is not a single chokepoint. Required surfaces are command dispatch, orchestrator instructions, worker packets/contracts, spec mirror, and tests. Reducer guards are explicitly retained in scope as invariants, not rewritten.
- **Secondary surfaces:** prep metadata law and report-packet schema are in scope because they control classification and ordering proof. Review/harden and non-UI worker routing remain out of scope.

### LBP Check
Restore the accepted structural contract using typed metadata, matching-cycle provenance, and regression tests. No external product/library choice exists; external-solution check skipped.

### Discovery Opportunity Scout
Skipped — narrow internal contract restoration; opportunity surface outside the accepted scope is zero.

### Recommended Objectives
1. Make `adv-engineer` the first implementation worker for classified UI/UX tasks.
2. Require a matching-cycle `adv-designer` correction/polish/alignment follow-up after successful implementation.
3. Make ordering and provenance machine-checkable without weakening completion or review gates.
4. Keep all policy surfaces and tests synchronized with the authoritative delegation law.

### AMBIGUITY ANALYSIS
No blocking ambiguity findings.

Coverage: B:C F:C S:C M:C

## Discovery Agenda Resolved
1. Regression identified: `669f124a` flipped the accepted routing law.
2. Current policy is multi-surface; the accepted engineer-first contract is the restoration target.
3. Inline, engineer-report, stale-cycle, and hint edge cases have explicit dispositions.
4. Ordering proof uses typed provenance and existing reducer guards.
5. Regression tests must assert semantics rather than stale text presence.
documents.problemStatement:
# Problem statement

The archived `updateSubagentDispatch` change established an engineer-first lifecycle for UI/UX work: `adv-engineer` implements code, then `adv-designer` performs a bounded UI/UX repair, polish, and alignment pass. Current Advance source instead routes `metadata.frontend == "true"` directly to `adv-designer`, contradicting that accepted dispatch contract.

Restore a structural, tested engineer-first → designer-follow-up lifecycle for explicitly classified UI/UX work. Preserve `adv-reviewer` as review/harden owner and keep the designer outside backend, API, storage, and business-logic scope.

# Agreement — Restore designer follow-up

## Objectives

1. Restore engineer-first, designer-follow-up lifecycle for every structurally classified UI/UX task.
2. Provide the smallest audited typed spec-delta operation needed to modify an existing requirement safely.
3. Restore the delegation law through that operation, not a direct global-spec edit.
4. Make ordering, provenance, delta validation, and failure behavior machine-checkable.
5. Preserve the root-cause evidence so future work does not mistake add-only delta support for complete spec-editing support.

## Success Criteria

- SC1: Every task with `metadata.frontend: "true"` has an engineer-first, designer-follow-up lifecycle.
- SC2: Delegated and risk-forced inline UI/UX implementation both produce verifiable designer follow-up or remain incomplete with explicit recovery state.
- SC3: A later edit cannot silently restore designer-direct initial implementation without semantic regression failure.
- SC4: An existing named requirement can be safely changed through a typed, audited modification delta and archive application.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: A delegated `type: code` task with `metadata.frontend: "true"` starts with `adv-engineer`; no initial direct-designer route remains.
- AC2: Successful classified implementation produces matching-cycle `adv-designer` follow-up with bounded engineer-result context.
- AC3: Successful inline classified implementation produces the same follow-up with bounded inline provenance.
- AC4: Classified designer reports reject missing, stale, or mismatched implementation-cycle provenance; existing completion guards remain enforced.
- AC5: Designer work remains UI-scoped, may align adjacent UI in the same surface, and reports broader work as follow-up.
- AC6: Unavailable preview evidence records reason plus bounded source/a11y review evidence.
- AC7: Delegation law, command/agent packets, documentation mirror, and semantic regression tests agree.
- AC8: `adv_delta_modify` accepts only a valid existing requirement target and validated change shape; unknown, duplicate, malformed, or conflicting target changes fail atomically.
- AC9: `rq-delDefaults10` is restored through the typed modify-delta path; archive is the sole global-spec writer.
- AC10: Durable change evidence records the separate causes of the add-only delta scope and the later designer-direct dispatch flip.

## Constraints

- C1: UI/UX classification is structural (`metadata.frontend`), never authoritative path/title/prose inference.
- C2: Designer follow-up receives implementation-cycle provenance and stays outside backend, API, storage, and business-logic scope.
- C3: Existing matching-cycle completion and stale-report rejection guards remain intact.
- C4: `adv-reviewer` remains sole review/harden owner.
- C5: Source changes land in `/home/jon/dev/advance`; deployed artifacts remain deploy-script outputs.
- C6: Scope is modify-only. Remove/rename/full CRUD delta operations remain out of scope.

## Avoidances

- DONT1: Do not route initial frontend implementation directly to `adv-designer`.
- DONT2: Do not weaken typed report validation or cycle provenance to make designer-direct routing pass.
- DONT3: Do not treat filename, component name, title, or free-form wording as authoritative UI/UX classification.
- DONT4: Do not expand designer corrections beyond adjacent UI alignment in the same surface without surfaced follow-up.
- DONT5: Do not directly edit global specs or add duplicate contradictory requirements as a substitute for modification support.

## Out of Scope

- OOS1: Model-routing policy or model selection.
- OOS2: Product-facing UI implementation.
- OOS3: Review/harden ownership changes.
- OOS4: Non-UI worker lane routing.
- OOS5: Remove, rename, or full CRUD spec-delta tooling.

## Preview Applicability

- visual_surface: false
- exact_route_required: not_applicable
- data_state_expectation: not_applicable
- viewport_expectation: not_applicable
- Rationale: orchestration/tooling change only; no product browser surface.

## Decisions

### User Decisions

- All tasks marked `metadata.frontend: "true"` receive mandatory designer follow-up.
- Unavailable preview permits documented bounded source/a11y fallback evidence.
- Designer may align adjacent UI only in the same surface.

# Design — Restore designer follow-up and safe spec modification

## Architecture Overview

Restore engineer-first → designer-follow-up UI delivery and add a narrow typed `adv_delta_modify` path. Modify records change-owned intent; archive remains sole global-spec writer and uses its existing generic modify engine.

## Key Decisions

1. Expose only `adv_delta_modify`; remove/rename/full CRUD stay out of scope.
2. Export and strengthen strict modify schemas: reject empty changes; validate capability-local target and replacement-scenario parents.
3. Mirror add-only lifecycle: validate → Signal → authoritative Query/read-back → projection. No direct global-spec write, Temporal Update, or second archive engine.
4. Classified UI work starts with engineer. Successful engineer and inline paths share one designer-follow-up builder.
5. Builder consumes returned durable `reportId`; `engineer_report` provenance must reference successful same-task/same-cycle engineer evidence.
6. Designer dispatch/report/verification failure records recovery and prevents task checkpoint completion.

## Implementation Strategy

1. Add modify schema exports/refinements, tool, tests, signal/payload, reducer appender, Temporal store operation, registry/policy/repoint/CLI/title/banner/preflight/doc entries.
2. Reuse archive modify application; record typed modification for `rq-delDefaults10`.
3. Restore engineer-first routing, hint boundary, shared follow-up builder, provenance referential checks, and failure handling.
4. Synchronize commands, agents, packet contracts, law/mirror, root-cause record, and semantic tests.

## Design-Derived Criteria

- DDC1: Non-empty, valid, capability-local modify changes reject invalid/unknown/duplicate/conflicting targets atomically at tool and reducer boundaries.
- DDC2: Only change-owned delta state mutates before archive; no direct global write.
- DDC3: No remove/rename/full-CRUD tools are registered.
- DDC4: Engineer-report provenance requires same task/cycle, `status: complete`, empty blockers, and successful required verification.
- DDC5: Delegated and inline classified UI work prove engineer-first → designer-follow-up; hints cannot select designer first.
- DDC6: Failed follow-up cannot checkpoint completion; stale/mismatch guards remain unchanged.
- DDC7: Tests cover delta validation/application, lifecycle order, provenance, hints, failures, and reviewer ownership.

## LBP Analysis

Expose the smallest missing control over existing typed archive capability. Reuse signals, read-back, report identity, implementation-cycle state, and archive dispatch; avoid heuristics, direct edits, second state machines, and full CRUD.

## Risks / Mitigations

- Invalid delta target → strict tool and reducer invariants.
- Incomplete engineer evidence → require completed status, no blockers, and passing required verification before designer handoff.
- Tool-surface drift → registry/policy/CLI/preflight/doc tests.
- False task completion → recovery evidence and no checkpoint after follow-up failure.

## Root-Cause Record

Add-only delta support was intentional and its modify follow-up was cancelled. `669f124a` separately flipped delegation law/mirror/test without touching delta tooling. Proven chains are distinct.

## Design Leverage Scout

Adopted: strict non-empty modify schema; target/scenario validation; returned report-ID handoff; same-task/cycle engineer referential check. Rejected: direct edits, Temporal Updates, new state machine, full CRUD.

## Independent Validation

Caution, no blockers. Validator confirmed modify-only path and existing archive/Temporal mechanisms are correct. Planning must implement and test: complete engineer-evidence predicate; tool and reducer modify invariants; unresolved designer failure cannot checkpoint completion.

The prior add-only delta surface could not safely correct the existing delegation requirement, and classified frontend work could start with the designer rather than the engineer. This change restores an auditable modify path and a verified engineer-result provenance chain before UI/UX follow-up.
